problem.name_latex: Maximum independent set, maximum clique and minimum vertex cover
problem.name: Maximum independent set, maximum clique and minimum vertex cover
problem.statement_latex:
Find $I\subseteq V$ of maximum size with no edge inside $I$. Equivalent exact objectives are maximum clique in the complement graph and minimum vertex cover $V\setminus I$ in the original graph. These equivalences preserve vertex count and translate witnesses directly.
The comparison uses quantum gate complexity and classical bit complexity on explicit graph inputs.
problem.statement_text: Find $I\subseteq V$ of maximum size with no edge inside $I$. Equivalent exact objectives are maximum clique in the complement graph and minimum vertex cover $V\setminus I$ in the original graph. These equivalences preserve vertex count and translate witnesses directly. The comparison uses quantum gate complexity and classical bit complexity on explicit graph inputs.

quantum.details_latex: This bound applies to maximum independent set on an arbitrary $n$-vertex graph. Complementation transfers it to maximum clique, and taking the complementary vertex set gives minimum vertex cover. Running the classical counting algorithm below on a quantum computer also supplies its subexponential upper bound.
quantum.details_text: This bound applies to maximum independent set on an arbitrary $n$-vertex graph. Complementation transfers it to maximum clique, and taking the complementary vertex set gives minimum vertex cover. Running the classical counting algorithm below on a quantum computer also supplies its subexponential upper bound.

classical.headline_latex: $\operatorname{poly}(n+|E|)2^{O(n\log\log n/\sqrt{\log n})}$, Boolean tensor contraction with cardinality constraints.
classical.headline_text: $\operatorname{poly}(n+|E|)2^{O(n\log\log n/\sqrt{\log n})}$, Boolean tensor contraction with cardinality constraints.
classical.details_latex: Use one Boolean variable per vertex and a width-two clause for each forbidden selected edge. A linear-size Boolean cardinality circuit tests the target size, so the encoding uses $O(n)$ variables and fixed-width clauses even for a dense graph. Exact counting and self-reduction recover an optimum in polynomial space. For sparse graphs, maximum independent set and minimum vertex cover have the sharper exponent $O(n/\sqrt{\log n})$; maximum clique has this sharper bound when its complement is sparse.

strength.description_latex: The subexponential classical bound is asymptotically smaller than the displayed amplified-branching quantum bound. The classical exponent is $n^{1-o(1)}$, so its exponential-to-subexponential reduction has no power saving.

evidence.description_latex: The stated algorithms have rigorous upper bounds. D\"orn's displayed bound supplies no asymptotic quantum-speedup claim against the current classical comparator.

hardware.description_latex:
The amplified branching method uses polynomial assignment and graph-evaluation workspace, with exponentially many coherent evaluations. Useful instances would require fault tolerance. The polynomial-space classical algorithm changes the relevant time comparison without adding an exponential memory requirement.
{\small [Before ``ETH is false'', the known general classical bound was $O^*(1.1996^n)$, and D\"orn's quantum algorithm claimed an improvement to $O^*(1.1488^n)$.]\par}
